questions.q: In `nvidia-smi dmon` output, GPU utilization repeatedly drops to 0% and spikes back up. What does this pattern usually indicate?
options: The GPU driver has crashed
The GPU is starved, typically waiting on a CPU-side bottleneck like the data loading pipeline
The kernel is compute-bound
Memory coalescing has failed
questions.explain: Utilization bouncing to near-zero repeatedly is the signature of a starved GPU — it's idle while waiting on something else, most often the dataloader.

questions.q: What is a classic cause of unnecessary host-device synchronization inside a training loop?
options: Using `DataLoader` with `pin_memory=True`
Calling `.item()` or `.cpu()` on a GPU tensor inside the hot loop, forcing the GPU to finish all queued work before the CPU can read the value
Using `torch.compile` on the model
Increasing the batch size
questions.explain: A `.item()` or `.cpu()` call forces a synchronization point, stalling the pipeline every iteration while the GPU finishes everything queued so far.

questions.q: After profiling a slow kernel with Nsight Compute, the 'speed of light' section shows high DRAM throughput and low compute throughput. What does this tell you?
options: The kernel is compute-bound and needs mixed precision
The kernel is memory-bound; fixing access patterns or fusing operations is the fix most likely to help
The kernel has a syntax error
The GPU is out of memory
questions.explain: High memory throughput paired with low compute throughput is the signature of a memory-bound kernel — the fix should target memory access, not raw compute.

questions.q: Why would applying mixed precision (Tensor Cores) fail to speed up a kernel that Nsight Compute identifies as memory-bound?
options: Mixed precision only works on CPUs
A memory-bound kernel is limited by memory bandwidth, not by compute throughput, so reducing compute time further doesn't address its actual bottleneck
Mixed precision always increases memory bandwidth usage
Nsight Compute cannot analyze mixed-precision kernels
questions.explain: Mixed precision speeds up compute throughput. A memory-bound kernel's ceiling is bandwidth, not compute, so that fix doesn't target the actual limiter.

questions.q: What is the recommended order of tools when diagnosing an unexplained slow training job?
options: Nsight Compute on every kernel first, then nvidia-smi to confirm
nvidia-smi to confirm the GPU is the bottleneck, then Nsight Systems for the timeline, then Nsight Compute on the specific slow kernel
Only Nsight Systems is ever needed
Rewrite the model from scratch before profiling anything
questions.explain: The practical workflow starts broad (nvidia-smi, then Nsight Systems) and narrows to Nsight Compute only once a specific kernel has been identified as worth a deep dive.
